title: Add a sprite to Tic-Tac-Toe
prompt:
Modify TempleOS's bundled game, ::/Demo/Games/TicTacToe.HC. Save your
version as B:/Home/RobotTicTacToe.HC on the writable RAM drive and
leave the original intact. Create B:/Home if needed. Save any separate
sprite assets on B: too; the boot drive is read-only.

Create a new 32x32 robot-face sprite: a yellow square face, two black
square eyes, a black horizontal mouth, and transparent space around
the face. Use a native TempleOS sprite, created in the sprite editor
or built in HolyC. Integrate it into the game as player 1's mark and
moving placement preview, replacing X. Keep player 2's O, the board,
turn order, occupied-square checks, and win detection working.

Run your saved game. Move the pointer to two empty squares and observe
the robot preview following it. Click the upper-left square to place
a robot. Click that occupied square again, then move the pointer off
the board to confirm that the placed mark has not changed. The turn
must also stay unchanged. Click the center square to place O, then
the upper-right square to place a second robot. Move the pointer off
the board and observe the two robots and one O.

Exit with Ctrl-Alt-C and launch B:/Home/RobotTicTacToe.HC again from the
shell. Confirm the board starts empty, then repeat the three valid
moves. Stop with robots in the upper-left and upper-right squares and
O in the center. Use real mouse clicks to play; do not set board values
in the shell.

grader.rubric:
Review the full source-edit, action, and screenshot trajectory.
The saved file must modify the bundled TicTacToe.HC, retaining its
game logic. Verify a new native sprite is rendered through TempleOS's
sprite API, rather than independent drawing over a board screenshot.
Accept either an editor-created asset or a sprite built in HolyC.

The sprite must have a 32x32 canvas, a yellow face, two black square
eyes, a black horizontal mouth, and transparency outside the face.
It must replace player 1's X both in placed marks and the live pointer
preview. Compare screenshots at two pointer positions before play
to verify preview motion. During play, moving the pointer must leave
placed marks fixed at their board cells. Player 2 must still use O.

Actual clicks must place a robot in the upper-left square, reject a
second click there without advancing the turn, place O in the center,
and place another robot in the upper-right square. Check that the
occupied click does not overwrite or add a mark and the next accepted
move is still player 2's. Game logic must preserve normal turn order,
occupied-square rejection, and win detection; inspect the source edit
for changes to those rules.

Require a visible exit to the shell and relaunch of the saved file,
an empty fresh board, and the repeated three valid moves. The final
board must show the two robots and center O. The original bundled
file must remain intact. Editing global board values, replacing the
game with a mockup, or showing art only in an editor does not satisfy
the task. Asset creation, source integration, live preview, placement,
rejection, and persistence are separately reviewable progress.

A final screenshot alone cannot prove source integration or persistence.
This task requires trajectory review and has no automatic pass score.
